findings.evidence: Page 34: "Code, numerics, and non-Latin scripts can run 2–5× (rule of thumb; the multiplier is tokenizer- and language-specific) the naive word-count estimate." The 2–5× range appears without any first-party or second-party provenance label. Per the Preface evidence discipline, every load-bearing quantitative claim needs Axis 1 and 2 labels. This 2–5× multiplier has no [2°], [1P], or [ILLUSTRATIVE] provenance tag.
findings.issue: Unlabeled quantitative claim: the 2–5× token multiplier for code/numerics/non-Latin scripts carries no evidence label despite being a load-bearing figure. The surrounding parenthetical acknowledges it is tokenizer-specific but does not supply provenance.
findings.fix_instruction: Add an evidence label pair, e.g. [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION], to the 2–5× figure in the bullet on page 34, consistent with how similar rule-of-thumb multipliers are handled elsewhere in the book.

findings.evidence: Page 32: "The vLLM FP8-KV blog post's often-quoted '54%' — from its Llama-3.1-8B Table 3 (vLLM blog, post dated 2026-04-22 — inside the 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff; retrieved 2026-11-15, an access date only, since access dates are not evidence dates, so no addendum revision applies) [S6] — is, on this book's reading of that table, a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope, not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient [1P][HYPOTHESIS]."
findings.issue: Provenance-label mismatch: the sentence labels the interpretation '[1P][HYPOTHESIS]', but [1P] is the Axis-1 provenance value meaning 'first-party: the model vendor's own spec'. The passage itself says the reading 'is the book's own, not a vendor-stated interpretation'. A book-authored reading of a third-party blog table is not a first-party vendor spec; under the book's own axis definitions (Preface: [1P] — first-party: the model vendor's own spec; [2°] — reputable second-hand: textbook, survey, or independent benchmark) the blog is a second-hand source relative to the book, and the book's own interpretation of it is not first-party at all. The same defect recurs in Ch 6 §6.6 (page 154): "the vLLM FP8-KV blog's '54%' [S6] is a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope, not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient — on this book's own reading of that post's Table 3, not a vendor-stated interpretation [1P][HYPOTHESIS]". Recurrence sweep: the identical '[1P][HYPOTHESIS]' label is also attached to 'the 8K end is an older-generation and small-tier deployment observation ... this book's reading of the vendor line-ups above, not a vendor statement [1P][HYPOTHESIS]' on page 27 — the same pattern of a book-authored reading being labelled first-party.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-label these three book-authored readings to a provenance value consistent with their source: use [2°][HYPOTHESIS] for the vLLM blog reading (second-hand source) and [canonical scenario][HYPOTHESIS] or [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] for the 8K-window reading, which is explicitly 'this book's reading ... not a vendor statement'. Reserve [1P] for the vendor's own stated figures. Sweep Ch 1, Ch 6 and Ch 7 for any other '[1P][HYPOTHESIS]' whose text disclaims vendor statement.
